title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk Audit

epigraph.quote: Order books tell you what customers intend to buy; working-capital days and cash conversion tell you on whose balance sheet the growth is being financed.
epigraph.author: Capital Goods Playbook

web_blocks.html: Eimco Elecon does not report unit volumes or equipment-versus-spares splits in its quarterly releases. Instead, investors must track five leading KPIs across presentations, BSE filings, and CRISIL reviews. First is the Open Order Book, followed by the Quarterly Revenue & EBITDA Margin Band. The other three are PSU vs. Private-Sector Mix, Active Installed Fleet & New Product Commercialization, and Working Capital Days & Capex Execution.

web_blocks.caption: Leading Operational KPIs & Trajectory (FY24–H1 FY27)
rows: Strong rebound in system-level order visibility.
Q2 FY27 jumped +70.9% YoY to ₹56.8 Cr; lumpy QoQ.
Working capital still absorbs cash (H1 FY27 CFO: ₹2 Cr).
Kanjari land & capacity expansion; maintenance capex from FY27.
web_blocks.takeaway: Order book (+202% YoY to ₹133 Cr) and H1 FY27 revenue (+33.3% YoY) confirm operational recovery, but H1 FY27 CFO of just ₹2 Cr shows growth is still working-capital intensive.

web_blocks.html: Structural Potential: Three catalysts shape Eimco Elecon's medium-term runway. First, Coal India aims to scale underground coal toward 100 MT, with 47 Continuous Miners now active across 27 CIL mines. That shift supports multi-year demand for the CM3500 package, shuttle cars, and roof bolters. Second, metal-mining growth backs 7T/10T LHDs and the new battery EVs (MCAR-E and UV-A-BE). Hindustan Copper plans to triple ore output from ~4.0 MTPA to 12.2 MTPA by FY30, while Hindustan Zinc is electrifying its fleet. Third, ICEMA expects 9–12% domestic construction equipment growth in FY27. That outlook gives EC-series piling rigs and the DW-220 wall grab an import-substitution runway backed by new capacity at Kanjari.

Order-Book Conversion, Capacity Ramp at Kanjari & PSU–Private Balancing: The order book shows both the demand rebound and the lumpiness of deliveries. In September 2025, deferred tenders pushed the backlog down to ₹44 Cr, pulling FY26 sales down 6.4% to ₹230.7 Cr. One year later, the open order book tripled (+202% YoY) to ₹133 Cr as of September 30, 2026. That backlog lifted H1 FY27 sales by 33.3% YoY to ₹134.3 Cr, including a 70.9% YoY jump in Q2 FY27 to ₹56.8 Cr. CRISIL also notes a big shift in the customer mix. Eimco moved from over 60–75% PSU reliance to a roughly 50:50 split between PSUs and private contractors/MDOs in FY26. To build CM3500 packages and piling rigs smoothly, management spent ₹60.5 Cr on FY26 capex, including Kanjari land. That spend lifted Net PPE from ₹64 Cr in March 2026 to ₹112 Cr by September 2026, with CRISIL expecting routine capex from FY27 onward.

Governance & Capital-Allocation Discipline Audit: Operational execution on the 18–20% EBITDA margin band and recent launches (CM3500, MCAR-E, UV-A-BE, DW-220) has been solid. Yet three governance signals need steady tracking. First, leadership is changing right as the plant expansion ramps up. Whole-time Director Mukulnarayan Dwivedi retired in September 2025 (succeeded by Kamlesh Nalin Shah), and CFO Vishal C. Begwani resigned effective October 30, 2026. Second, in December 2025, shareholders amended the Memorandum of Association (MoA) to allow entry into defence platforms, embedded systems, pharmaceuticals, and medical gear. Those fields have zero engineering overlap with heavy mining machinery. Third, cash conversion stays weak: H1 FY27 produced just ₹2 Cr of CFO on ₹25 Cr of EBITDA as working capital absorbed ₹16 Cr.

Execution Bridge — From Order Book to Plant Utilization: The ₹133 Cr open order book as of September 2026 gives roughly two quarters of revenue visibility, up sharply from ₹44 Cr a year earlier. With H1 FY27 sales already at ₹134.3 Cr, the key test for FY27–FY28 is throughput at the expanded Vallabh Vidyanagar and Kanjari plants. Management must turn CM packages, metal-mine LHDs, and DW-220 wall grabs into billed deliveries while holding the 18–20% EBITDA margin band. Avoiding capital diversion into the December 2025 MoA items like defence or medical gear is just as important. Staying focused on core machinery will decide whether this cycle yields lasting operating leverage.

CEO & Management Walk-the-Talk Audit: Leadership under Executive Director Prayasvin B. Patel (Chairman & MD of Elecon Engineering) and Whole-time Director Kamlesh Nalin Shah shows a mixed but improving record. Where they delivered: management guided for 18–20% medium-term EBITDA margins and hit 18.6% in FY26 and 18.5% in H1 FY27 despite a 6.4% FY26 sales dip. They balanced the customer mix from >60–75% PSU dependence to ~50:50 PSU-private in FY26. They also completed a clean Sandvik exit and launched four local products: CM3500, MCAR-E, UV-A-BE, and DW-220. Where skepticism is warranted: first, the FY25 annual report noted that long-term mine performance for the local CM package was still being proven. Second, CFO Vishal C. Begwani resigned effective October 30, 2026. Third, the December 2025 MoA expansion into defence, embedded systems, pharma, and medical gear risks distracting capital from heavy engineering.

web_blocks.mechanism: In Indian industrial capex, order-book surges only translate into durable returns on capital when management avoids unrelated diversification and enforces working-capital discipline as revenue scales.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Elecon Engineering's MHE division endured a >10-year margin and working-capital slump post-2011 before restructuring around products/aftermarket, lifting MHE revenue +72.8% YoY in FY25 while Gears aftermarket/spares exceeded 30% of division sales.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Sister-group Elecon Engineering already generates ~30%+ of its Gear division revenue from aftermarket/spares and exports globally; Eimco Elecon is still early in building non-coal/export scale and recently added unrelated MoA objects (pharma/medical/defence) that must be watched for focus drift.

book_paragraphs: When you and I track a capital-goods manufacturer, we cannot wait for audited annual earnings to tell us what happened six months ago. We need leading operational indicators that flash early. For Eimco Elecon, the cleanest forward signal is the open order book, which tripled—jumping 202% year-on-year—to ₹133 crore as of September 30, 2026, up from a trough of ₹44 crore a year earlier. That backlog translated directly into H1 FY27 revenue of ₹134.3 crore, up 33.3% year-on-year, with Q2 FY27 surging 70.9% to ₹56.8 crore at an 18.8% EBITDA margin.

Equally important is who is signing the purchase orders. Five years ago, Eimco Elecon was overwhelmingly dependent on Coal India and Singareni Collieries. By FY26, CRISIL confirms that the revenue mix between public-sector undertakings and private-sector Mine Developer-cum-Operators and infrastructure contractors had balanced out at roughly 50:50. That diversification reduces single-buyer dependence, even though private-sector contractors introduce their own tender and site-clearance timing swings.

Now let us conduct an honest walk-the-talk audit of management under Prayasvin B. Patel and Whole-time Director Kamlesh Nalin Shah. On engineering and margin discipline, leadership deserves real credit: they guided for an 18% to 20% medium-term EBITDA margin band and delivered 18.6% in FY26 and 18.5% in H1 FY27 despite FY26's 6.4% revenue dip. They executed a clean, amicable separation from Sandvik without losing the 'Eimco' brand, and they delivered four major indigenous products in a single stretch—the CM3500 Continuous Miner, the MCAR-E and UV-A-BE battery EVs, and the DW-220 Diaphragm Wall Grab.

book_subsections.title: Three Governance & Capital-Allocation Watchpoints You Cannot Ignore
paragraphs: Even with strong engineering execution on the shop floor, three yellow flags deserve your close attention. First, key financial leadership is in transition right as the expanded Kanjari and Vallabh Vidyanagar capacity comes online: CFO Vishal C. Begwani resigned effective October 30, 2026, barely a year after Whole-time Director Mukulnarayan Dwivedi's retirement. You and I want to see a seasoned industrial CFO appointed quickly to steward working capital.

Second, in December 2025, Eimco Elecon amended its corporate charter—its Memorandum of Association—to add defence platforms, embedded systems, pharmaceuticals, and medical equipment. We saw in sister-company Elecon Engineering's Material Handling Equipment division how a decade-long post-2011 slump only ended when management stripped out distractions and refocused on core products and aftermarket spares. Expanding into pharma or medical gear would stray far from heavy mining machinery; we must watch closely to ensure it remains a dormant legal clause rather than an actual capital sink. Third, H1 FY27 cash conversion was sluggish at just ₹2 crore of operating cash flow on ₹25 crore of EBITDA, proving that working-capital discipline remains unfinished business.

book_subsections.title: From ₹44 Crore to ₹133 Crore: Reading Order-Book Momentum Without Blind Spots
paragraphs: Let us put ourselves in the shoes of an industrial operator looking at Eimco Elecon's order-book swings over the past three years. In December 2023, the open order book stood at a healthy ₹152 crore. By March 2025 it had cooled to ₹86 crore, and by September 2025 it had dipped all the way to ₹44 crore as PSU and private-sector tenders got stuck in approval queues. That air pocket showed up directly in FY26's 6.4% revenue decline. Then, within twelve months, the backlog roared back 202% to ₹133 crore in September 2026—fueling a 70.9% revenue surge in Q2 FY27 alone.

What does that whiplash teach you and me? First, never extrapolate a single trough quarter like September 2025 or a single boom quarter like Q2 FY27 into a straight-line trend. Instead, watch two things together: order-book conversion speed and capital discipline. With ₹60.5 crore of FY26 capex now sitting in ₹112 crore of net fixed assets, the Kanjari and Vallabh Vidyanagar expansion is built. Management no longer has an excuse of capacity constraints—the plant must now deliver higher throughput while keeping EBITDA margins anchored in the 18% to 20% band.

At the same time, keep a sharp eye on the executive suite. With CFO Vishal C. Begwani stepping down in October 2026 and the company now operating independently of Sandvik, disciplined financial stewardship is more vital than ever. If management stays laser-focused on mining, foundation rigs, and spares—and leaves the unrelated pharma and medical clauses in its amended charter untouched—this order book can translate into genuine operating leverage.

book_subsections.title: What to Listen For in Management's Next Four Quarters
paragraphs: As you and I monitor Eimco Elecon over the coming year, let us boil our checklist down to four concrete operational signals that cut through corporate noise. First, track the conversion of the ₹133 crore September 2026 order book into quarterly revenue—and watch whether fresh order inflows replenish the backlog above ₹120 crore rather than sliding back toward FY26's ₹44 crore trough. Second, watch the mix between Coal India PSU orders and private Mine Developer-cum-Operators, ensuring that private-sector growth does not come with stretched payment defaults.

Third, watch for the appointment of a strong permanent Chief Financial Officer following Vishal C. Begwani's October 2026 departure, and check whether H1 FY27's sluggish ₹2 crore operating cash flow rebounds as finished machines are delivered and commissioned. Fourth, read every quarterly filing and capital-expenditure note for any sign that management is deploying money into the December 2025 MoA additions—defence, embedded systems, pharmaceuticals, or medical equipment. As long as capital stays concentrated in Vallabh Vidyanagar, Kanjari, underground mining, and foundation rigs, Eimco Elecon remains a focused industrial franchise; any capital drift outside that circle is an immediate yellow flag.

Finally, when you evaluate management’s track record, pay attention to what did not happen during the 2025 Sandvik separation. Often, when a foreign co-promoter exits a three-decade joint venture via an Offer for Sale, the departing partner strips away brand rights, triggers non-compete disputes, or leaves the Indian entity scrambling for working-capital credit. Here, Tamrock Great Britain Holdings exited its 24.68% stake cleanly in September 2025, raised no objection to Eimco Elecon keeping the Eimco brand name, and CRISIL subsequently reaffirmed the company’s A/Stable credit rating in August 2026. That smooth transition gives Prayasvin Patel and Kamlesh Shah a clean runway—now execution on working capital and core focus must do the talking.

Above all, remember that in cyclical capital goods, order-book quality matters as much as order-book size: a ₹133 crore backlog backed by funded Coal India and Tier-1 infrastructure contracts is worth far more than speculative private orders prone to site delays.

In short, Eimco Elecon has built the physical capacity and launched the indigenous products needed for India’s underground coal and foundation-rig upcycle; now its operational KPIs will show whether execution matches ambition.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: The Unrelated-Objects Litmus Test
book_callouts.text: When a cash-rich, debt-free engineering company adds 'pharmaceuticals and medical equipment' to its corporate charter, don't panic—but don't ignore it either. Watch the next four quarters of capex and R&D disclosures to verify that capital stays anchored in mining, piling rigs, and aftermarket spares.
